correctness.rationale: Conditioning on K=k makes the occupied labels a uniform k-subset and the labeled resample a uniform surjection onto that subset. Merging a fixed pair of draw positions gives the collision probability S(b-1,k)/S(b,k), which determines the diagonal and off-diagonal second moments of the bootstrap weights. The centered-data identity then yields the conditional variance. The global covariance is independently reconstructed from exact multinomial count moments with absent-cell indicators. Boundary cases k=1 and k=b agree with, respectively, repeated copies of one observation and simple random sampling without replacement. Exact enumeration over all small draw sequences reproduces every displayed formula.

value.rationale: The number of represented original observations is a classical measure of bootstrap information content and directly motivated fixed-support resampling methods. The theorem quantifies that motivation exactly for the most basic bootstrap statistic: it gives the full finite conditional variance at every support level and an explicit negative covariance between support diversity and squared mean error. The endpoint strata connect ordinary bootstrap resampling to one-point repetition and simple random sampling without replacement, making the identity a structural calibration rather than an arbitrary moment calculation.
